import Mathlib.Tactic
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.ModEq

/-- IMO 1964 P1 (a): `7 ∣ 2 ^ n - 1` iff `3 ∣ n`, for positive `n`. -/
theorem p09_a (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : 7 ∣ 2 ^ n - 1 ↔ 3 ∣ n := by
  constructor
  · -- Forward direction: if 7 ∣ 2^n - 1, then 3 ∣ n
    intro h
    have h₁ : 2 ^ n % 7 = 1 := by
      have h₂ : 7 ∣ 2 ^ n - 1 := h
      have h₃ : 2 ^ n % 7 = 1 := by
        rw [← Nat.mod_add_div (2 ^ n) 7]
        omega
      exact h₃
    -- Use the fact that 2^n mod 7 has period 3
    have h₂ : n % 3 = 0 := by
      have h₃ : ∀ k : ℕ, 2 ^ k % 7 = 1 ↔ k % 3 = 0 := by
        intro k
        induction' k with k ih
        · simp
        · cases k with
          | zero => simp
          | succ k' =>
            simp [pow_succ, Nat.mul_mod, Nat.add_mod] at *
            omega
      have h₄ := h₃ n
      simp [h₁] at h₄
      omega
    exact Nat.dvd_of_mod_eq_zero h₂
  · -- Backward direction: if 3 ∣ n, then 7 ∣ 2^n - 1
    intro h
    have h₁ : n % 3 = 0 := Nat.mod_eq_zero_of_dvd h
    have h₂ : 2 ^ n % 7 = 1 := by
      have h₃ : ∀ k : ℕ, 2 ^ k % 7 = 1 ↔ k % 3 = 0 := by
        intro k
        induction' k with k ih
        · simp
        · cases k with
          | zero => simp
          | succ k' =>
            simp [pow_succ, Nat.mul_mod, Nat.add_mod] at *
            omega
      have h₄ := h₃ n
      simp [h₁] at h₄
      omega
    have h₃ : 7 ∣ 2 ^ n - 1 := by
      have h₄ : 2 ^ n % 7 = 1 := h₂
      have h₅ : 2 ^ n ≥ 1 := by
        apply Nat.one_le_pow
        linarith
      omega
    exact h₃

/-- IMO 1964 P1 (b): no positive `n` has `7 ∣ 2 ^ n + 1`. -/
theorem p09_b (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : ¬7 ∣ 2 ^ n + 1 := by
  intro h
  have h₁ : 2 ^ n % 7 = 6 := by
    have h₂ : 7 ∣ 2 ^ n + 1 := h
    have h₃ : (2 ^ n + 1) % 7 = 0 := by
      omega
    have h₄ : 2 ^ n % 7 = 6 := by
      omega
    exact h₄
  -- Show that 2^n mod 7 can never be 6
  have h₂ : ∀ k : ℕ, 2 ^ k % 7 ≠ 6 := by
    intro k
    have h₃ : ∀ m : ℕ, 2 ^ m % 7 ∈ ({1, 2, 4} : Set ℕ) := by
      intro m
      induction' m with m ih
      · simp
      · cases m with
        | zero => simp
        | succ m' =>
          simp [pow_succ, Nat.mul_mod] at *
          omega
    have h₄ := h₃ k
    simp at h₄
    omega
  have h₃ := h₂ n
  contradiction
```

import Mathlib.Tactic.IntervalCases
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith

/-- IMO 1964 P1 (a): `7 ∣ 2 ^ n - 1` iff `3 ∣ n`, for positive `n`. -/
theorem p09_a (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : 7 ∣ 2 ^ n - 1 ↔ 3 ∣ n := by
  -- We work with congruences modulo `7`.
  have h7 : (2 ^ 3) ≡ (1 : ℕ) [MOD 7] := by
    -- `2³ = 8 ≡ 1 (mod 7)`.
    have : 7 ∣ 2 ^ 3 - 1 := by norm_num
    exact (Nat.modEq_iff_dvd).mpr this
  constructor
  · intro h
    -- From the divisibility we get a congruence.
    have hmod : (2 ^ n) ≡ (1 : ℕ) [MOD 7] :=
      (Nat.modEq_iff_dvd).mpr h
    -- Write `n = 3 * q + r` with `r < 3`.
    obtain ⟨q, r, hqr, hr⟩ := Nat.mod_mul_left_divisible n 3
    have hpow : (2 ^ n) ≡ (2 ^ r) [MOD 7] := by
      -- Using `n = 3 * q + r` and the fact that `2³ ≡ 1`.
      have : (2 ^ (3 * q)) ≡ (1 : ℕ) [MOD 7] := by
        have := h7.pow q
        simpa [Nat.pow_mul] using this
      have : (2 ^ n) ≡ (2 ^ (3 * q) * 2 ^ r) [MOD 7] := by
        have := (Nat.ModEq.rfl : (2 ^ (3 * q + r)) ≡ (2 ^ (3 * q + r)) [MOD 7])
        simpa [hqr, Nat.pow_add, Nat.mul_comm, Nat.mul_left_comm, Nat.mul_assoc] using this
      simpa [Nat.mul_comm, Nat.mul_left_comm, Nat.mul_assoc] using
        (this.trans ((Nat.ModEq.mul_left _ this).trans (Nat.ModEq.mul_right _ this))).trans
          ((Nat.ModEq.mul_left _ this).trans (Nat.ModEq.mul_right _ this))
    have : (2 ^ r) % 7 = 1 := by
      have := congrArg (fun x => x % 7) hmod
      simpa [hpow] using this
    -- Now analyse the possible values of `r`.
    have hr0 : r = 0 := by
      interval_cases r using hr
      · rfl
      · have : (2 ^ 1) % 7 = 2 := by norm_num
        linarith
      · have : (2 ^ 2) % 7 = 4 := by norm_num
        linarith
    -- Conclude that `3 ∣ n`.
    exact ⟨q, by
      simpa [hqr, hr0, Nat.zero_mul, Nat.add_zero]⟩
  · intro h
    rcases h with ⟨k, rfl⟩
    -- Show that `2 ^ (3 * k) ≡ 1 (mod 7)`.
    have hpow : (2 ^ (3 * k)) ≡ (1 : ℕ) [MOD 7] := by
      have := h7.pow k
      simpa [Nat.pow_mul] using this
    -- Hence `7 ∣ 2 ^ (3 * k) - 1`.
    exact (Nat.modEq_iff_dvd).mp (by
      simpa using hpow)

/-- IMO 1964 P1 (b): no positive `n` has `7 ∣ 2 ^ n + 1`. -/
theorem p09_b (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : ¬7 ∣ 2 ^ n + 1 := by
  -- Suppose otherwise.
  intro h
  -- From the divisibility we obtain a congruence.
  have hmod : (2 ^ n) ≡ (-1 : ℕ) [MOD 7] :=
    (Nat.modEq_iff_dvd).mpr h
  -- As in part (a) we have `2 ^ n ≡ 2 ^ (n % 3)`.
  obtain ⟨q, r, hqr, hr⟩ := Nat.mod_mul_left_divisible n 3
  have hpow : (2 ^ n) ≡ (2 ^ r) [MOD 7] := by
    have : (2 ^ (3 * q)) ≡ (1 : ℕ) [MOD 7] := by
      have h3 : (2 ^ 3) ≡ (1 : ℕ) [MOD 7] := by
        have : 7 ∣ 2 ^ 3 - 1 := by norm_num
        exact (Nat.modEq_iff_dvd).mpr this
      have := h3.pow q
      simpa [Nat.pow_mul] using this
    have : (2 ^ n) ≡ (2 ^ (3 * q) * 2 ^ r) [MOD 7] := by
      have := (Nat.ModEq.rfl : (2 ^ (3 * q + r)) ≡ (2 ^ (3 * q + r)) [MOD 7])
      simpa [hqr, Nat.pow_add, Nat.mul_comm, Nat.mul_left_comm, Nat.mul_assoc] using this
    simpa [Nat.mul_comm, Nat.mul_left_comm, Nat.mul_assoc] using
      (this.trans ((Nat.ModEq.mul_left _ this).trans (Nat.ModEq.mul_right _ this)))
  have : (2 ^ r) % 7 = 6 := by
    have := congrArg (fun x => x % 7) hmod
    simpa [hpow] using this
  -- Analyse the possible values of `r`.
  interval_cases r using hr
  · have : (2 ^ 0) % 7 = 1 := by norm_num
    linarith
  · have : (2 ^ 1) % 7 = 2 := by norm_num
    linarith
  · have : (2 ^ 2) % 7 = 4 := by norm_num
    linarith
